title: FindLink: Learning to Assess Scientific Connections from Source-Grounded Premises
abstract: arXiv:2611.02545v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Scientific discovery from the literature requires assessing connections among findings obtained under different study conditions. Source attribution makes individual findings traceable, but does not determine what they jointly support. We introduce GI-TraceBench, a benchmark of 10,282 questions in gastrointestinal oncology that unifies provenance question answering, knowledge discovery, and hypothesis evaluation through shared Paper, Claim, and Evidence Span records. We further propose FindLink, a two-stage framework for provenance-grounded scientific reasoning. Premise Grounding constructs source-bound premises with explicit study context and support status. Structured Reasoning organizes these premises into support plans that represent both supported relations and unresolved conditions, then generates evidence-conditioned answers using deterministic compiler feedback. translated_title: FindLink：基于来源锚定前提学习评估科学关联
translated_abstract: arXiv:2611.02545v1 公告类型：新论文。摘要：基于文献的科学发现需要评估在不同研究条件下所得发现之间的关联。来源归因使单个发现可追溯，但并不能确定它们共同支持什么。我们提出 GI-TraceBench，一个包含 10,282 个问题的胃肠肿瘤学基准，通过共享的论文、主张和证据片段记录，统一了来源溯源问答、知识发现和假设评估三类任务。我们进一步提出 FindLink，一个面向来源锚定科学推理的两阶段框架。前提锚定阶段构建带有明确研究背景和支持状态的来源绑定前提；结构化推理阶段将这些前提组织成同时表示支持关系与未决条件的支持计划，并利用确定性编译器反馈生成以证据为条件的答案。该编译器验证结构与来源绑定的一致性，但……（原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出 GI-TraceBench 基准与 FindLink 两阶段框架，通过构建来源锚定前提并进行结构化推理，结合确定性编译器反馈，来评估不同研究条件下科学发现之间的关联。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces GI-TraceBench and FindLink, a two-stage framework that grounds source-bound premises and performs structured reasoning with deterministic compiler feedback to assess connections among scientific findings obtained under different study conditions.
